text:
Greetings dear colleagues,
Just now, the relief planner mentioned a point about handover calls

I need to flag this urgently for the Companion Animal Travel Desk because the last stretch of routine desk work has shown how easy it is for small gaps to turn into animal welfare problems. When we pass a booking from one shift to another, we have to keep the notes plain, complete, and calm. That means every handler needs the same picture of the carrier setup, feeding note, comfort item, and any warning signs from the traveler or the station team. If the handover is thin, the next person may waste valuable attention chasing basics instead of watching the animal.

Please keep using the humane approach that Aurelia Skyways expects on every route between skyports. The desk should never sound rushed to the passenger, even when the queue is building. If a pet appears stressed, we slow the pace, check the crate carefully, and make sure the next update is sent before the file moves on. Leila Mori and Theo Clark are good reminders that travelers notice tone as much as process, and the same is true for the animal beside them. Finn was handled well on the last run because someone stayed patient and wrote down the small details that mattered.

I am asking everyone to treat handover calls like a safety step, not an extra chore. Say what changed, what stayed the same, and what still needs watching. Keep the language direct, keep the note trail readable, and speak up right away if a concern is not being carried forward. That is how we protect dependable companion travel and keep the desk steady.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
